searchText: Indeed, that would be important to clarify, becuse it seems to me there is confusion about that. - testing performance boundaries does not need multiple clients. It will always test an implementation, not a spec. It will ideally be a spec compliant implementation, and ideally a spec that is complete - testing interop is a very different things. It can show spec holes, it can show perforamnce regressions from different interpretations of the spec or from different implementation decisions. Indeed, that would be important to clarify, becuse it seems to me there is confusion about that.
- testing performance boundaries does not need multiple clients. It will always test an implementation, not a spec. It will ideally be a spec compliant implementation, and ideally a spec that is complete
- testing interop is a very different things. It can show spec holes, it can show perforamnce regressions from different interpretations of the spec or from different implementation decisions. But it is a different game
